1.?

Which of the following is equivalent to log81⁡x?

H
Mon, Mar 24th @ 10:08 AM|Elapsed: 1:16Correct

We use the change of base formula: loga⁡X=logb⁡Xlogb⁡a

We want to change from base a=81 to base b=3. So, we have

log81⁡x=log3⁡xlog3⁡(81).

Rewriting the expression in the denominator using exponents, we get

log3⁡xlog3⁡(81)=log3⁡xlog3⁡(34)=log3⁡x4.

Therefore, we conclude that

log81⁡x=log3⁡x4=14log3⁡x.

2.?

Which of the following is equivalent to log36⁡x?

H
Mon, Mar 24th @ 10:10 AM|Elapsed: 1:47Correct

We use the change of base formula: loga⁡X=logb⁡Xlogb⁡a

We want to change from base a=36 to base b=6. So, we have

log36⁡x=log6⁡xlog6⁡(36).

Rewriting the expression in the denominator using exponents, we get

log6⁡xlog6⁡(36)=log6⁡xlog6⁡(62)=log6⁡x2.

Therefore, we conclude that

log36⁡x=log6⁡x2=12log6⁡(x).

3.?

Use a calculator to evaluate log22⁡(20) rounded to 3 decimal places.

E
Mon, Mar 24th @ 10:12 AM|Elapsed: 0:43Correct

Let's calculate log22⁡(20) by changing the base 22 to the common logarithm (base 10).

We use the change of base formula: loga⁡X=logb⁡Xlogb⁡a

In our case, a=22, X=20, b=10. So, we have

log22⁡(20)=log10⁡(20)log10⁡(22)=log⁡(20)log⁡(22)≈1.3010301.342423≈0.969

In our case, a=8, X=30, b=10. So, we have

log8⁡(30)=log10⁡(30)log10⁡(8)=log⁡(30)log⁡(8)≈1.477120.90309≈1.64
